contentBody: **In data analysis, what does "hallucination" specifically refer to?**
option.1: An AI refusing to answer any question involving numbers
option.2: A chart rendering with the wrong colours
option.3: A dataset that has been encrypted before upload
option.4: An AI stating a number, trend, or cause that is not actually supported by the data it was given
answerExplanation: Hallucination in data analysis means confidently stating something — a wrong average, an invented trend, an unsupported cause — that the source data does not actually back up.

contentBody: **A dataset shows that students who join a study group also tend to get higher grades. Which statement is the safest to write in a report?**
option.1: "Joining a study group is associated with higher grades in this data; a causal link is not yet proven."
option.2: "Joining a study group causes higher grades."
option.3: "Grades have nothing to do with study groups."
option.4: "Every student must join a study group starting next term."
answerExplanation: The data shows a correlation. Students who join study groups might already be more motivated for other reasons — writing "causes" without further testing overstates what the data can prove.

contentBody: **An AI claims a defect rate of "about 20%" after being told 18 out of 675 units failed inspection. What should you do before repeating that number?**
option.1: Trust it immediately — AI arithmetic is always correct
option.2: Recompute it yourself: 18 ÷ 675 ≈ 2.7%, and flag the large discrepancy
option.3: Round it up further to 25% to be safe
option.4: Remove the defect metric from the report entirely rather than check it
answerExplanation: 18 ÷ 675 is approximately 2.7%, not 20% — a sanity check that takes seconds and prevents a small, real number from being reported as something far more alarming.

contentBody: **A backend approval step takes 48 hours on average before a user can proceed. A teammate says, "This 48-hour wait must be a broken screen in the app — let's redesign it." What does validating domain logic suggest here?**
option.1: Agree immediately and redesign the screen the user sees during the wait
option.2: Assume the AI invented the 48-hour figure and ignore it
option.3: Check whether the 48 hours is actually a backend review process rather than a UI problem before proposing a redesign
option.4: Domain logic is irrelevant once a number has been verified
answerExplanation: A number can be arithmetically correct and still be misdiagnosed. Validating domain logic means asking whether the proposed cause actually matches how the real process works — a backend review delay is not fixed by a screen redesign.

contentBody: **Which of these is a genuinely "decision-ready" recommendation in a report?**
option.3: "The data looks interesting; more research is needed."
option.4: "Send a one-tap loyalty-signup prompt to every customer within 48 hours of their first purchase, and track signup rate over the next four weeks."
answerExplanation: A decision-ready recommendation names a specific, buildable action and a way to check whether it worked. The other options are vague enough that no team could act on them directly.
